description: A modular Kiro Power giving developers unified, AI-assisted access to the fragmented geospatial landscape across open, free-tier, and proprietary sources. Built on a dual-fragmentation framing where data access (Pillar A) and processing/compute (Pillar B) receive equal weight, plus a GeoAI pillar (Pillar C).

companions.name: gdal-mcp
companions.relationship: Recommended companion (third-party). Not part of this Power and not redistributed with it; the user installs it separately from PyPI under its own license.
companions.identity: gdal-mcp - GDAL/Rasterio operations MCP server (Wayfinder-Foundry / JordanGunn)
companions.license: MIT (the companion project's own license; see its repository)
companions.complements: Local-file GDAL processing (workspace-scoped) that complements this pack's cloud-native connectors: file-level raster/vector reprojection and conversion, and common vector ops (buffer, simplify, clip) not covered by geo-ops.
caveats: Operates on local files scoped by GDAL_MCP_WORKSPACES (a colon-separated allowlist of directories). If unset, all paths are allowed - set it to constrain access.
Includes a reflection middleware: methodology-sensitive tools (reprojection, resampling, query extent) require a structured justification before they execute.

servers.name: kiro-geospatial
servers.role: Power Hub: Onboarding Dashboard, Resource Catalog, Credential Manager (single mcp.json surface), Orchestration Router.

servers.name: geo-common
servers.uvx: (installed as a dependency of every server)
servers.role: Shared base package: single async httpx HTTP client, RetryPolicy + exponential backoff, rate-limit handling, Error_Taxonomy, BaseGeoServer.

servers.name: geo-stac
servers.role: STAC catalog search and asset discovery across Earth Search (Element84), MS Planetary Computer, NASA CMR-STAC, Copernicus Data Space, USGS.

credentials.description: Optional subscription key that raises Planetary Computer rate limits; open access works without it.
Optional NASA Earthdata bearer token used only for access-restricted collections.

servers.name: geo-vector
servers.role: Vector features for a spatial extent from OpenStreetMap (Overpass) by default; Overture Maps is supported as an optional, explicitly configured GeoJSON endpoint (Overture has no public REST API - its data is cloud-native GeoParquet queried via DuckDB).

servers.name: geo-geocode-route
servers.role: Address-to-coordinate geocoding and reverse geocoding (Nominatim, Photon), routing (OSRM, Valhalla), and isochrones (Valhalla); Amazon Location is a credentialed geocoder selectable via source=amazon-location.

credentials.description: API key for the Amazon Location geocoder, selected via source=amazon-location; the open providers (Nominatim/Photon/OSRM/Valhalla) work without it.

servers.name: geo-terrain
servers.role: Elevation, slope, and hillshade from SRTM (default) and USGS 3DEP via the public OpenTopoData endpoint; the source endpoint/dataset is overridable to point at a self-hosted instance.

credentials.description: Optional API key for OpenTopography-hosted datasets; other open DEM sources work without it.

servers.name: geo-weather-climate
servers.role: Weather, climate, and environmental observations from Open-Meteo (default), OpenAQ, and NOAA/NWS (US); NOAA Climate Data Online when configured. ERA5 reanalysis is covered via the Open-Meteo archive (ERA5-derived), not a direct Copernicus CDS client.

credentials.description: NOAA CDO API token; required only for the credentialed 'cdo' source (selectable via source=cdo). Open-Meteo/OpenAQ/NWS work without it.

servers.name: geo-biodiversity
servers.role: Species occurrence records from GBIF, iNaturalist, IUCN.

credentials.description: Optional token for authenticated iNaturalist queries; GBIF open access works without it.
IUCN Red List API v4 account token; enables the opt-in 'iucn' source (select via source=iucn) for taxon conservation-status lookups. GBIF/iNaturalist occurrence search works without it.

servers.name: geo-ops
servers.role: CRS transforms, geometry validation/operations, spatial joins, overlay, buffer and convex hull via PyProj, Shapely/GEOS, GeoPandas. Local, pure-function logic.

servers.name: geo-formats
servers.role: COG / GeoParquet / Zarr / COPC conversion and validation via GDAL, rio-cogeo.

credentials.description: Optional AWS credentials for reading or writing cloud-optimized outputs on S3; local file I/O works without them.
Optional AWS secret paired with AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID.

servers.name: geo-query
servers.role: Spatial SQL over data in place via DuckDB Spatial (open, geo-query[duckdb]) and Amazon Athena (geo-query[athena], wired when AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID is set). Both ship as concrete engines.

credentials.description: Optional AWS credentials for the Athena engine (install geo-query[athena]); the DuckDB Spatial engine works without them.
Optional AWS secret paired with AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID.
S3 staging location for Athena query results (s3://...). Required to run the Athena engine; an optional ATHENA_DATABASE sets the default Glue database.

servers.name: geo-raster
servers.role: Windowed Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF reads, band math (NDVI/NDWI/NBR), and zonal statistics over rasters via byte-range reads (rasterio/rioxarray, rasterstats, TiTiler).

credentials.description: Optional AWS credentials for private S3 raster assets; public assets work without them.
Optional AWS secret paired with AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID.

servers.name: geo-pointcloud
servers.role: Cloud-Optimized Point Cloud (COPC) read/write and streaming via PDAL.

credentials.description: Optional AWS credentials for private S3 point-cloud assets; public assets work without them.
Optional AWS secret paired with AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID.

servers.name: geo-index
servers.role: H3 (resolutions 0-15) and S2 (levels 0-30) spatial indexing via h3 and s2geometry. Local, pure-function logic.

servers.name: geo-foundation-models
servers.role: Geospatial foundation-model embeddings, segmentation, and change detection via Clay, Prithvi-EO-2.0, SatCLIP, SAMGeo.

credentials.description: Optional Hugging Face token for gated model weights; openly licensed models load without it.

servers.name: geo-embedding-search
servers.role: Embed, index, and run semantic/similarity search via OpenSearch and LanceDB.

credentials.description: Optional OpenSearch endpoint; the default LanceDB local store works without it.
Optional OpenSearch username paired with OPENSEARCH_URL.
Optional OpenSearch password paired with OPENSEARCH_URL.

servers.name: geo-warehouse
servers.role: Spatial SQL at warehouse scale against BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, and Databricks. All four ship as concrete engines (geo-warehouse[bigquery|redshift|snowflake|databricks], each wired when its *_CONNECTION/credential is set). Connection secrets live in the *_CONNECTION env (a JSON object or a path to a JSON file); the per-call connection argument is the non-secret database/schema. Processing/compute-class (counts toward Pillar B). First expansion module.

credentials.license_reference: Requires a Google Cloud BigQuery account (the free BigQuery sandbox is sufficient for testing). See Google Cloud terms.
credentials.description: Service-account credential for BigQuery: either the path to a service-account JSON key file or the JSON itself. The connection argument is the GCP project id. Install the geo-warehouse[bigquery] extra to enable the concrete engine. If your org blocks service-account keys (iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation), use Application Default Credentials instead: run `gcloud auth application-default login` and set BIGQUERY_USE_ADC=1 (no key file needed).

credentials.license_reference: Requires a Snowflake account/subscription. See Snowflake terms of service.
credentials.description: Snowflake connection as a JSON object (or a path to a JSON file): account, user, and an auth credential (password, or the more secure private_key_file / authenticator for key-pair / SSO-OAuth), plus optional warehouse/role/schema. The connection argument is the database. Install geo-warehouse[snowflake].

credentials.license_reference: Requires an Amazon Redshift cluster/serverless workgroup. See AWS terms.
credentials.description: Redshift connection as a JSON object (or a path to a JSON file): host/port/user/password, or the more secure IAM auth (iam:true with cluster_identifier/region/db_user, or is_serverless). TLS is enforced. The connection argument is the database. Install geo-warehouse[redshift].

credentials.license_reference: Requires a Databricks workspace and personal access token. See Databricks terms.
credentials.description: Databricks connection as a JSON object (or a path to a JSON file): server_hostname + http_path of the SQL warehouse, plus access_token (PAT) or OAuth client_id/client_secret; optional catalog. The connection argument is the schema. Install geo-warehouse[databricks].

servers.name: geo-commercial-imagery
servers.role: Commercial imagery discovery and ordering, routed by provider: Maxar WorldView via the Sentinel Hub Third-Party Data Import (TPDI) API, and Planet (PlanetScope/SkySat) via Planet's own Data + Orders APIs. Sentinel Hub TPDI is being sunset for Planet data and no longer offers Airbus, so Planet uses its first-party APIs and Maxar stays on TPDI. Maxar orders are create-only by default; Planet orders are placed on confirm.

credentials.license_reference: Requires a Sentinel Hub commercial subscription with Maxar access. See https://www.sentinel-hub.com/.
credentials.description: Sentinel Hub OAuth client id (Maxar via TPDI).

credentials.license_reference: Requires a Sentinel Hub commercial subscription with Maxar access. See https://www.sentinel-hub.com/.
credentials.description: Sentinel Hub OAuth client secret (Maxar via TPDI).

credentials.license_reference: Requires a Planet account/subscription and API key. See https://docs.planet.com/.
credentials.description: Planet API key for the Planet Data + Orders APIs (PlanetScope/SkySat).

servers.name: aws-geo-compute
servers.role: Peer Power for heavy/distributed compute: deterministic task-type to execution-target mapping over AWS Batch, Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate, Amazon EMR with Apache Sedona, and Amazon SageMaker AI. Ships a concrete AWS Batch backend (aws-geo-compute[aws]) covering the Batch and Fargate targets, wired when AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID is set and AWS_BATCH_JOB_QUEUE/AWS_BATCH_JOB_DEFINITION are configured; Amazon EMR and Amazon SageMaker AI remain bring-your-own-backend. Engine selection and planning always run offline.

credentials.description: AWS access key id used to submit AWS Batch, AWS Fargate, Amazon EMR, and Amazon SageMaker AI jobs and read/write S3 outputs. Optional: engine selection and planning run offline; enforced at job submit/status time.
AWS secret paired with AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID. Optional; enforced at job submit/status time.
AWS region in which compute jobs run. Optional; enforced at job submit/status time.

servers.name: geo-ogc
servers.role: Fetch GeoJSON features for a spatial extent from any OGC API - Features service (pygeoapi, GeoServer OGC API, ldproxy) by endpoint + collection id.

servers.name: geo-3d
servers.role: 3D geospatial formats: inspect/validate OGC 3D Tiles tilesets and glTF/GLB assets, tile point clouds into 3D Tiles (.pnts), and mesh DEM grids into glTF/GLB terrain. Local, dependency-free.

skills.name: cloud-optimized-formats
skills.description: When to use COG/GeoParquet/Zarr/COPC and how to write cloud-optimized outputs.

skills.name: crs-handling
skills.description: Always track CRS; reproject explicitly; avoid silent axis-order bugs.

skills.name: tool-selection
skills.description: Decision tree for choosing the right server/engine for a task and data size.

skills.name: spatial-sql
skills.description: Run spatial SQL across engines: pick geo-query vs geo-warehouse, and use the right ST_* function names per engine.

skills.name: stac-metadata
skills.description: Proper STAC item/asset metadata: datetime, bbox, collections.

skills.name: tiling
skills.description: Dynamic tiling, overview levels, and web-mercator pyramids.

skills.name: geoai-embedding
skills.description: GeoAI embedding workflow: tile -> model -> embedding -> index.

steering.name: cog-conversion
steering.description: read raster -> validate -> to_cog (overviews) -> verify pixel-exact round-trip -> write to silver/gold.

steering.name: zonal-statistics
steering.description: load raster + vector zones -> align CRS -> zonal_statistics -> handle no-data zones -> emit GeoParquet.

steering.name: stac-discover-analyze
steering.description: stac_search -> select assets -> windowed read_window -> analyze -> summarize provenance.

steering.name: embedding-change-detection
steering.description: tile two dates -> embed_tile (same model) -> detect_change -> threshold/report.

pillarReconciliation.rule: Across the combined MVP + expansion set, the count of Pillar B (processing/compute) MCP servers SHALL be no fewer than the count of Pillar A (data-access) MCP servers.

pillarB_processing.note: Six native Pillar B servers plus geo-warehouse (processing-class, warehouse-scale spatial SQL). The aws-geo-compute peer Power adds further processing weight but is not counted here.
